newsitem.title: CANADA: Royal Bank sees rise in consumer spending.
newsitem.headline: Royal Bank sees rise in consumer spending.

text.p: Canadian consusmer spending is poised to pick up in 1997, the results of a recent survey show, the Royal Bank of Canada said on Thursday.
Canada's largest bank said a recent survey conducted for it by the Angus Reid Group seems to confirm that low interest rates and rising consumer confidence are encouraging Canadians to spend more.

"This year we should see the gradual strengthening of consumer confidence in Canada. We've already seen some encouraging signs like the rebound in the housing market, and now consumer spending in general is poised to pick up," said Royal Bank chief economist John McCallum in a statement.
The survey found Canadians named vacations as their top spending priority for 1997, and the travel and tourism industries should be big winners this year, the bank said.
Contributions to registered retirment savings plans (RRSPs) were ranked as the second highest spending priority, followed by furniture or appliances, cars and home renovations.
The Royal Bank cautioned that while consumer spending should pick up, any hope of a return to the free-spending 1980s is misplaced and "consumers are returning to the fold gradually."
